purpose: Synthetic examples and question bank for a Malaysian emergency triage app prototype; not a clinical decision rule or validated training set.

sources.assessment_questions: Emergency Nursing: 5-Tier Triage Protocols, 2nd ed., Appendix B, uploaded PDF 9780826137913_ap02.pdf
sources.ats_scenarios: Australian Emergency Triage Education Kit, Chapter 10, uploaded PDF emergency_triage_education_kit_-_chapter_10_-_triage_scenarios.pdf

zone_note: Zone mapping is an app design proposal, not an official equivalence; actual physical treatment zones vary by hospital. Level 2 may be managed in a different area locally. Time targets describe the cited 2019 scale, not estimated queue waits.

question_bank.prompt: Is the person awake and breathing normally?
Can they speak in full sentences?
Is there severe chest pain, severe breathing difficulty, a seizure now, a new weakness or speech problem, major bleeding, or a serious injury?
What is the main problem, in your own words?
When did it begin and is it getting worse?
Where is the pain and how severe is it from 0 to 10?
Have they fainted, become confused, or had a change in alertness?
Are they pregnant or could they be pregnant? If yes, how many weeks?
Is there fever, vomiting, dehydration, a rash, or bleeding?
What medical conditions, medicines and allergies are relevant?
How did the injury happen and when? Was there a head injury or loss of consciousness?
Are you thinking of harming yourself or someone else, and do you have a plan or means available now?
Record measured heart rate, respiratory rate, blood pressure, temperature and oxygen saturation, if available.
Record observed consciousness, work of breathing, skin colour, perfusion and active bleeding.
Where is the patient now and can they travel safely?

agent_output_schema.routing_allowed_rule: Only after a clinician confirms low acuity and current receiving-hospital capacity, services, travel time and acceptance; never route level 1-3 based on the app alone.

synthetic_cases.presentation: Severe breathlessness; speaks single words; oxygen saturation reported below 90% on room air
Adult with severe ongoing chest pain and sweating
Pregnant adult with fever, shortness of breath, short phrases and oxygen saturation 90%
Severe flank pain radiating to groin; cool and clammy despite pain medication
New one-sided weakness and slurred speech
Child with abdominal pain, vomiting once and persistent distress despite paracetamol
Toddler recovered from a first seizure with fever, now alert
Person says they may jump off a bridge if problems do not improve, currently cooperative

implementation_notes: Ask first-look safety questions before any lengthy intake; interrupt the interview for emergency signals.
Never infer absent vital signs are normal; capture units, measurement source and time.
Preserve original Australian ATS category separately if adding further education-kit scenarios.
Reassess when symptoms worsen, answers conflict, or the patient has waited; keep clinician override and audit history.
Hospital recommendations must use verified live capacity, relevant services, travel times and acceptance; empty beds alone do not prove suitability.
Do not use these synthetic examples to claim model accuracy or make autonomous patient diversion decisions.
